t: #2309 Greatest English Letter in Upper and Lower Case — Editorial
o:
Find the largest letter of the alphabet that appears in `s` in both cases; return it uppercase or empty string.

'lEeTcOdE' has only E/e in both cases → 'E'. 'arRAzFif' has A/a, F/f, R/r → greatest is 'R'. 'AbCdEfGhIjK' has no letter in both cases → ''.

Length ≤ 1000, alphabet size 26 — collect case-insensitive presence and scan from Z down.
k: Build two presence sets: lowercase letters seen and uppercase letters seen.
Scan 'Z' down to 'A' and return the first letter present in both sets.

a.n: Approach 1: Presence Sets + Reverse Alphabet Scan
a.i: Record which letters appear lowercase and which appear uppercase; iterate the alphabet from Z to A returning the first letter in both sets.
s: For c from 'Z' to 'A', if c in uppercase set and c.lower() in lowercase set, return c.
a.t: O(n + 26) — one pass to build sets, constant scan.

w: Simplest possible approach and optimal. Alternative: bitmask ints for lower/upper presence and take `low & (up << 32)` style tricks, or in Python `set(s) & set(s.upper())` mapped to uppercase then max(). Pitfall: remembering to return UPPERCASE and the empty-string fallback.
